name: set_global_value_32
description: Stores the constant 32 into a global variable and returns. It is a one-instruction routine called from a single caller, so it only initialises that variable.

name: advance_timer_spawn_object
description: When a flag is set, the routine clears it, advances an animation counter that wraps around, and decrements a countdown timer. When the countdown reaches zero it writes a new entry into a table with fixed field values and a position derived from stored coordinates, then resets the timer.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_key
description: Once the pending flag is set, it reads a keyboard byte from the CIA-A serial data register, shifts out its bits and records a pressed or released state in a per-key table. It clears the pending state and then waits until the flag is set again.

name: acknowledge_keyboard_handshake
description: Clears a stored key value and one table byte, waits until the keyboard pending flag is set, then clears the flag and sets it to a fixed value. It uses the CIA-A control and interrupt registers and is called from a single routine.

name: update_object_table_entries
description: Initialises a set of counters and then walks a table of object entries until it reaches an end marker. Each entry is moved by its stored step, dispatched by a type code and retired when it leaves the visible area or reaches its limit, and some global counters are advanced along the way.

name: add_packed_decimal_score
description: Adds a packed decimal value into a score byte with decimal adjustment and carry propagation. When the sum's low digit is non-zero it sets a pending update flag and keeps only the upper digit.

name: store_entry_in_slot
description: If a pending slot index is valid, the flag bit is clear and the x coordinate is aligned to eight units within a window around a reference position, it writes the coordinate into that slot with an offset, writes a fixed value into a second table entry and a marker value into a third field. It then clears the pending slot index.

name: draw_active_entries_bitplanes
description: Loops over thirty eight-byte table slots, decrementing each slot's timer and clearing expired entries. Entries inside the visible window that sit close to a reference column set two state variables, and their pixel patterns are ORed into several positions in the bitplane buffers.

name: fill_pending_motion_entry
description: Fills the pending table slot with a new entry: scaled and offset x and y positions taken from the inputs, two timer values chosen from the type input, and two motion fields derived from differences against reference values. It then clears the pending slot index.

name: advance_and_plot_entries
description: Loops over fifteen eight-byte entries, moving each by its stored step and removing entries that leave the visible range or reach a limit. Entries still on screen are drawn as shaded patterns into several bitplane buffers, and an entry close to a reference column sets two state variables.

name: swap_bitplane_buffers
description: Toggles a screen flag and saves the three current bitplane pointers into backup variables. It then assigns new bitplane pointers and base values for the selected buffer and calls another routine.

name: clear_screen_with_blitter
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, then sets its masks, modulo and control word so only the destination channel is used with the logic function set to zero. It points the destination at a bitplane and starts a fixed-size blit, which clears that bitplane.

name: run_copper_setup_sequence
description: Calls six routines in order and returns, with no data handling of its own. The sequence includes the copper list start, which points the copper at a new copper list.

name: store_constant_table_pairs
description: Writes six fixed pairs of values into a block of global variables, each pair a value followed by a second constant, and returns. The values are constants, so the routine only initialises a table of entries.

name: install_handler_enable_interrupts
description: Stores the address of a handler routine in a global vector variable and writes an enable mask to the interrupt enable register with the top bit set, so the listed interrupt sources are switched on.

name: configure_cia_timer_interrupt
description: Stores a handler routine address and writes a sequence of constants to the CIA-A control, interrupt and timer registers, configuring a timer interrupt. It finishes by clearing one bit of a stored control byte.

name: dispatch_two_subroutines
description: Calls two routines in order and returns. It has no register or data access of its own.

name: save_view_and_hardware_state
description: Calls a routine, then stores the current view and copper list pointers and the DMA control and interrupt enable register values into global variables. It also calls the graphics library's LoadView function.

name: disable_all_dma_and_interrupts
description: Writes a value with every bit set except the top one into the DMA control and interrupt enable registers, which clears those enable bits. The same value is also stored into a global variable.

name: restore_saved_hardware_state
description: Clears the DMA and interrupt enable bits, then restores the saved copper list pointer and DMA and interrupt enable values with the top bit set so they are re-enabled. It waits until a status bit in a global variable is set, calls the graphics library's LoadView function, and then closes the library.

name: open_graphics_library_retry
description: Repeatedly calls the exec library open function until it returns a non-zero library base, then stores that base in a global variable. It is written as a retry loop with no limit on attempts.

name: open_dos_library_retry
description: Repeatedly calls the exec library open function until it returns a non-zero library base, then stores that base in a different global variable. It is written as a retry loop with no limit on attempts, and it is aimed at the DOS library.

name: close_library_base
description: Calls the exec CloseLibrary function on the library base held in a global variable and returns.

name: start_program_parse_arguments
description: Program entry point that allocates a working structure, copies the command-line arguments into a buffer and splits them into a table of strings, handling quoted text and escape codes. It then runs the main routine and cleans up, returning an error code if the allocation fails.

name: release_working_resources
description: Stores its argument in a working structure, then closes an open file and a library if they are present, frees the structure's memory with task switching disabled and replies to a message. It returns the stored argument.

name: run_pager_session
description: Opens a window and runs the pager session, reporting errors such as a failed window open, a file that is not found or an end of file. It warns when a file may contain binary data and loops over pages until the quit key is pressed.

name: apply_to_four_entries
description: Calls a routine four times, each time passing a field from the input structure together with one of four consecutive global values in turn.

name: check_buffer_for_binary
description: Calls a read routine to fill an eighty-byte buffer, then scans it and returns 1 if any byte is a control code other than tab, newline or form feed, or 0 when every byte looks like text.

name: read_pager_key_command
description: Waits for a pending input event with a timeout and returns early when a break signal arrives. It then reads one key code and selects a command from the code's range, and codes outside the known set mark an error and return a failure value.

name: call_routines_then_jump
description: Calls two routines in sequence, then jumps through a pointer held in an address register. The decompiler shows no more of the body, so only this sequence is recovered and the jump target is unknown.

name: initialize_state_run_steps
description: Sets an activity counter to one and clears a flag in a state block, then calls a routine and stores its result. It runs a stepping routine repeatedly while the counter stays positive and a pair of values in a linked structure show that work remains.

name: update_state_increment_counter
description: Calls two routines, passing the second one a field from the state block and the result of the first, and stores the second result back in the block. When a flag in the block is zero it increments a short counter in a linked structure.

name: read_buffer_find_line_end
description: Reads up to 128 bytes into a buffer, scans for the first newline or form feed, and returns the number of characters up to and including it. A form feed is replaced by a visible caret-L and newline pair, and a flag in the state block is set.

name: run_pager_loop_until_quit
description: Chooses a loop count from state flags, then repeats a step that passes each table entry to a routine and reads a key. The loop quits when the key is q or a break code.

name: search_text_until_found
description: Selects a search buffer from a flag, prepares the search pattern and repeatedly fetches the next line and tests it until a match is found, then returns one. It shows a Searching message while it works.

name: wrap_call_with_setup
description: Performs a fixed sequence of calls around a main call, with an extra call when a field is set, and returns the result of the main call.

name: call_pair_repeat_if_clear
description: Calls a routine with two arguments, then calls it again with only the first argument when a flag in the state block is clear.

name: call_with_window_field
description: Calls a routine with a stored pointer, a value and a fixed argument, then calls another routine with a short field read from a linked state block.

name: call_with_window_minus_one
description: Calls a routine with a fixed zero value and a one, then calls it again with the window field from a linked state block minus one.

name: draw_text_buffer_lines
description: Walks a text buffer and outputs up to the requested number of lines in chunks of at most 128 characters. It stops early at a line feed or form feed and finishes by passing the remaining text to the output routine.

name: call_then_forward_pointer
description: Calls a routine with the second argument, then calls another routine with a pointer field from that structure, the address of a global variable and the first argument.

name: set_flag_and_forward
description: When the field at offset four is zero it first sets a short counter in a linked structure to one. It then calls a routine with a pointer field from the structure and the address of a global variable.

name: dispatch_by_flag
description: Calls a routine with a stored pointer, a global variable address and a second value. The second value is the global variable address when the flag is zero, otherwise it is one more than a short field in a linked structure.

name: call_with_flag_arguments
description: Calls a routine with a stored pointer and a global variable address. It passes the global address three times when the flag is zero, or passes a short field from a linked structure as the third argument otherwise.

name: clamp_negative_result
description: Calls a routine twice with the same first argument and different third arguments, then clamps a negative result to zero and returns it.

name: consume_from_buffer
description: Transfers up to the requested count of bytes from a buffer at a stored offset into the caller's destination, limited by the remaining size. If too little data remains it first calls a routine to refill the buffer, then advances the offset and position fields and reduces the remaining size by the amount moved.

name: refill_buffer_window
description: Returns zero early when a state field is not at its full value and pending data exists. Otherwise it writes out the pending bytes through a routine, reads a new block of up to 4096 bytes and adds the count to the fill size, then resets the offset and copies saved positions back into the state.

name: update_window_position
description: Computes a target position from the argument and the structure's offset fields, then compares it with the window start and length. When the target lies outside the window it resets the offsets and calls routines to reposition, otherwise it updates the offset and remaining size fields, and it returns the previous position or minus one for an invalid mode.

name: read_line_from_buffer
description: Reads characters one at a time through a routine into a destination string until a newline arrives or a fixed limit of about 127 characters is reached. It then writes a null terminator over the end of the text and returns the number of characters read.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination one at a time, including the terminating null, and stops once the null has been copied.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Walks a null-terminated string in place and changes each lowercase ASCII letter to uppercase by subtracting the case offset. Other characters are left unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign and then accumulates decimal digits from a null-terminated string, returning the signed integer value. It stops at the first character that is not a digit.

name: call_library_with_mask
description: Calls a library function through a base pointer held in a structure, passing the base, the argument and an all-bits-set value. It does nothing when the structure pointer or the library base is missing.

name: print_message_and_reset
description: Passes the structure's fields through a series of routine calls, writing the message string when one is given or running the default handler when it is empty. When a wait flag is set and the text is non-empty it reads input until a newline arrives, then restores saved fields and releases the structure through library calls.

name: send_one_byte_message
description: Stores its argument in a one-element stack buffer and passes that buffer, with a size of one, to a routine together with a handle from a lookup and a constant code. It returns the result of that call.

name: copy_allocated_block_fields
description: Allocates a block of 36 bytes and reads two fields from it into the caller's structure, using the result of an intermediate call to select the source. It frees the block afterwards and returns the intermediate result, or zero when the allocation fails.

name: create_linked_object_copy
description: Allocates a 68-byte block, links it to a handle obtained from a routine and copies a given number of words from a source into it. It then passes the new block to another routine and returns one of its fields, or zero when the allocation fails.

name: forward_with_stack_pointer
description: Calls another routine with its two arguments and a pointer to a fixed location in the caller's stack frame, then returns.

name: extract_byte_from_call
description: Calls a routine to fill a one-byte stack buffer and returns that byte as a number when exactly one byte was produced, or minus one otherwise.

name: format_and_forward_text
description: Calls the exec formatting routine through a library base held in a global variable, then measures the null-terminated text left in a 140-byte stack buffer. When the text is not empty it passes the buffer and its length to another routine.

name: divide_32_bit_values
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor, using a bit-by-bit long division when the divisor is wider than 16 bits and a 16-bit divide otherwise. It returns the quotient and remainder packed into one 64-bit result.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products and combines them into a 32-bit product. The second returned value is the multiplier with its two halves swapped.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls a single routine and returns, with no data handling of its own. It is reached only through a gap in the code, so its purpose is unknown.

name: negate_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and returns its first result, negated when the second result register is non-zero.

name: invoke_formatting_routine
description: Calls the exec formatting routine through a function pointer stored in a global variable and returns. It takes no arguments of its own.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into the memory location held in an address register and returns. It is a small writer used by a caller that supplies the destination pointer.

name: allocate_message_entry
description: Allocates a signal bit and, if that succeeds, allocates a memory block for a message. It fills the message's type, reply signal and value fields, then passes it to a routine, or frees the signal again when the allocation fails.

name: release_message_port
description: Removes the port from a list when it is linked, marks it as deleted and frees its signal bit, then releases the 34-byte memory block.

name: find_substring_in_string
description: Searches a null-terminated string for a second string, trying each starting position in turn, and returns one when the second string is found. It returns zero when the second string is empty, the first string begins with a newline, or no match exists.

name: initialize_self_linked_header
description: Stores the block's own address into its first word, advances that pointer by four, clears the next word and stores the block address into the word after it. The result is a self-referencing list header.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is given, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base structure into it. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: scan_list_and_build_block
description: Program entry: walks a linked list to find the largest value, then creates a block sized from that value and fills it with an increasing sequence of values. It copies sixteen words into the block and stores a handler routine address in it, returning zero on success or minus one when a lookup fails.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is given, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base structure into it. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: scan_list_and_build_block
description: Program entry: walks a linked list to find the largest value, then creates a block sized from that value and fills it with an increasing sequence of values. It copies sixteen words into the block and stores a handler routine address in it, returning zero on success or minus one when a lookup fails.

name: copy_sixteen_words_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is given, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in a base structure into it. It then calls a routine through a function pointer.

name: start_program_parse_arguments
description: Program entry point that allocates a working structure, copies the command-line arguments into a buffer and splits them into a table of strings, handling quoted text and escape codes. It then runs the main routine and cleans up, returning an error code if the allocation fails.

name: release_working_resources
description: Stores its argument in a working structure, then closes an open file and a library if they are present, frees the structure's memory with task switching disabled and replies to a message. It returns the stored argument.

name: start_resident_tool
description: Applies the same XOR byte twice to a hidden string, which restores the original text, then looks up a resident tool and starts it. It reports when the tool cannot be found or started and returns after the report.

name: compare_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte and returns minus one when the first is smaller, one when it is larger, or zero when they match.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of linked entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each and storing a value from a routine in it. Each node is linked to the next, and the first node is returned, or the list built so far when an allocation or lookup fails.

name: call_forbid_function
description: Calls the exec Forbid function through the library base held in a global variable, which disables task switching, and returns.

name: call_permit_function
description: Calls the exec Permit function through the library base held in a global variable, which re-enables task switching, and returns.

name: call_alloc_mem_function
description: Calls the exec AllocMem function through the library base held in a global variable and returns the allocated address.

name: call_find_task_function
description: Calls the exec FindTask function through the library base held in a global variable and returns its result.

name: call_put_message_function
description: Calls the exec PutMsg function through the library base held in a global variable and returns.

name: call_get_message_function
description: Calls the exec GetMsg function through the library base held in a global variable and returns the message it obtains.

name: call_wait_port_function
description: Calls the exec WaitPort function through the library base held in a global variable, which waits for a message on a port, and returns its result.

name: call_close_library_function
description: Calls the exec CloseLibrary function through the library base held in a global variable and returns.

name: call_open_library_function
description: Calls the exec OpenLibrary function through the library base held in a global variable and returns the library base it opens.

name: call_library_entry_624
description: Calls a library function at a fixed offset from the library base held in a global variable and returns its result. The function is not identified in the executable.

name: append_release_suffix_text
description: When the buffer's character at a fixed position is a two, it compares the buffer with a reference string and, once the reference is fully matched, writes a dot and four spaces after a fixed offset and returns. Otherwise it steps through the buffer while it matches the reference string.

name: write_dot_and_padding
description: Writes a dot followed by four space characters into a buffer at a fixed offset, with no other effect.

name: skip_matching_prefix
description: Advances through a buffer while its characters match a reference string, stopping at the first mismatch or at the end of the reference.

name: return_without_action
description: Does nothing and returns, with no register or memory access. It is a no-op routine referenced by three callers.

name: call_reschedule_function
description: Calls the exec Reschedule function through a pointer held in a global structure and returns.

name: call_dispatch_function
description: Calls the exec Dispatch function through the library base held in a global structure and returns.

name: call_alloc_mem_function
description: Calls the exec AllocMem function through the library base held in a global variable and returns the allocated address.

name: forward_with_stack_pointer
description: Calls another routine with its two arguments and a pointer to a fixed location in the caller's stack frame, then returns.

name: format_and_forward_text
description: Calls the exec formatting routine through a library base held in a global variable, then measures the null-terminated text left in a 140-byte stack buffer. When the text is not empty it passes the buffer and its length to another routine.

name: store_byte_through_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into the memory location held in an address register and returns. It is a small writer used by a caller that supplies the destination pointer.

name: dispatch_through_unrecovered_jump
description: Program entry that calls a library function, then jumps through a table whose targets the decompiler could not recover. Its own work is limited to that call and that jump.

name: start_program_write_background_color
description: Program entry point that writes to the background colour hardware register and calls four routines. The decompiler timed out, so the full sequence is not recovered.

name: store_byte_and_return_shifted
description: Reads a longword from just before an address register, writes a word made from a byte of it and the high byte of a second argument through a pointer, and returns the longword halved with its top bit set.

name: shift_bit_buffer_refill
description: Shifts a bit register right once per iteration for a count taken from an argument, and calls a routine to refill the register whenever it runs empty. It returns once the count is exhausted.

name: initialize_ram_unit_from_list
description: Opens a library and walks a linked list of unit entries looking for one whose name matches a stored string. For a match it copies the unit's parameters, allocates a buffer, fills a table of values, sets pointers into the new unit and links it into a unit list, returning zero on success.

name: build_ram_unit_structures
description: Copies unit parameters, allocates a buffer for the unit's data, and fills a 128-entry table with an increasing sequence while zeroing the following block. It sets a few header fields, stores the negated sum of the table as a checksum and returns zero.

name: copy_words_then_build_unit
description: Copies a block of words from a source into a destination, then builds the unit structures in the same way as its neighbouring routine. It allocates a buffer, fills its table and stores a checksum, returning zero on success.

name: initialize_ramdrive_device
description: Stores pointers to internal buffers and control fields and links the new unit into a global list while interrupts are masked. It then fills a 128-entry table with a sequence derived from a global value, sets flags and a checksum, and returns zero.

name: free_memory_blocks_twice
description: Calls the exec FreeMem function twice through the library base held in a register, then returns zero.

name: allocate_matching_list_entry
description: Masks interrupts while it walks a linked list for entries whose flags contain the requested bits, records a value from a matching entry that reaches the threshold, and passes the result to an exec library routine. It restores the interrupt state before returning.

name: scan_matching_list_entries
description: Walks a linked list for entries whose flags contain the requested bits and, once a qualifying value is found, calls an exec library routine with it. It masks interrupts while scanning and returns the call's result.

name: decrement_interrupt_nest_count
description: Decrements a nesting count stored in the device base and re-enables interrupts through a global write when the count falls below one. It returns zero.

name: store_value_at_offset
description: Stores the data register value at a fixed offset inside a structure given in an address register, then returns zero.

name: dispatch_device_message
description: Disables task switching, selects a handler from a table of sixteen entries using a code in the message, and stores that handler's result in the message. It replies to the message when a flag is clear, then re-enables task switching.

name: return_minus_three_constant
description: Returns the constant minus three with no other effect.

name: unlink_and_free_unit_node
description: Decrements a counter in a unit structure and, when it goes negative while a link is pending, unlinks the node from its list and releases its memory through the exec library. It then calls a library function to finish.

name: remove_unit_and_append_colon
description: Copies a field to the destination, removes a node from a unit list and calls a library function. It then appends a colon to the name in the buffer and calls the Permit function.

name: terminate_string_with_colon
description: Copies a longword into a destination, calls a library function, then advances to the end of a string and replaces its terminating null with a colon before calling the Permit function.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Library entry point of the math library that contains only an unimplemented instruction, so the decompiler stops here and no behaviour is recovered.

name: store_pointer_in_global
description: Stores the address register argument into a global variable and returns, as a routine of the math library.

name: unlink_and_free_library_node
description: If a short field is zero, it unlinks the structure from its list and frees its memory through the exec library, then returns a stored result. Otherwise it sets the bit with value eight in the structure's flag byte and returns zero.

name: mark_structure_pending_flag
description: Sets the bit with value eight in a flag byte inside the structure and returns zero.

name: open_math_library_first_use
description: If the flag bit with value eight is clear, it increments a use counter and, on the first use, stores the exec base and opens the library named in the text. It returns the structure pointer, or minus one when the flag bit is set.

name: return_minus_one_constant
description: Returns minus one with no other effect.

name: decrement_counter_and_call
description: Decrements a short counter in the structure. When the counter reaches zero and the flag bit with value eight is set, it calls a routine and records its result, and when the counter reaches zero it also calls a routine with the saved base.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls a single routine and returns, with no data handling of its own.

name: compute_mantissa_bit_loop
description: Returns at once for a zero input and passes a negative input to a routine. Otherwise it shifts the value and runs a bit-by-bit loop that builds a result from the set bits, returning when the working difference reaches its limit.

name: adjust_bitfield_value
description: Sets a bit in a value chosen by a count, then runs a loop that doubles a difference and shifts a mask until the count runs out. It increments the value when the difference meets a condition and returns the value combined with a byte of the count.

name: call_and_adjust_status_bits
description: Calls a routine through the math library and returns its result with the bit of value eight cleared and the bit of value two set.

name: call_math_entry_sequence
description: Calls nine library entries through the math library base, alternating between two of them and calling a third entry once in the middle, then returns.

name: compare_values_adjust_result
description: Calls several math library entries to compare and classify two operands, choosing one of several call sequences from the outcomes. It returns its result with the bits of value two and eight adjusted.

name: select_math_sequence_result
description: Calls math library entries to test two operands and selects one of several call sequences based on the outcome. It returns a result with the bits of value two and eight adjusted.

name: select_math_entry_by_sign
description: Calls a math library entry, then selects further entries based on a sign flag and a second value. It returns the result of the final call with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: select_entries_by_two_flags
description: Chooses among a few math library entries based on two flags and a sign value, then returns the result of a further call with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: choose_math_entry_by_sign
description: Calls a math library entry, then chooses between two or three further entries based on a sign value and a second flag. It returns the final call's result with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: call_entry_then_mask_result
description: Calls one math library entry, then returns the result of a further call with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: call_entry_twice_mask_result
description: Calls the same math library entry twice, then returns the result of a further call with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: mask_return_value
description: Calls a math library entry twice, then returns the result of a further call with the bits of value two and eight cleared.

name: close_library_base
description: Calls the exec CloseLibrary function on the library base held in a global variable and returns.

name: open_library_base
description: Calls the exec OpenLibrary function through the library base held in a global variable and returns.

name: divide_mantissa_bit_loop
description: Calls a routine when the exponent is large, then runs a 24-step bit loop that subtracts shifted values to build a quotient. It calls another routine when the loop overflows and returns.

name: run_quotient_bit_loop
description: Runs the same 24-step subtract-and-shift loop on its argument to build a quotient, and calls a routine when the loop overflows before returning.

name: execute_loop_with_branching
description: Runs a shift-and-subtract loop that decrements a counter each step. When the counter runs out it calls a routine, and it calls a second routine on that exit path when a flag byte is set before returning.

name: compute_cordic_style_value
description: Reduces its angle argument by fixed constants, then runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants, as used for trigonometric values. It calls a routine with the result and then returns.

name: compute_cordic_range_checked
description: Returns early when the argument is outside a set range. Otherwise it reduces the argument by fixed constants, runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants, and calls two routines with the result.

name: compute_cordic_then_call
description: Reduces the argument by fixed constants and runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants. It then calls a routine with the result and returns.

name: compute_cordic_signed_result
description: Returns early when the argument is outside a set range. Otherwise it reduces the argument, runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants, and calls routines whose path depends on a sign value passed on the stack.

name: compute_cordic_accumulate_only
description: Reduces the argument, runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants and calls one routine with the result, with no branch on sign.

name: compute_cordic_with_sign_branch
description: Reduces the argument, runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants, and then branches on a sign value passed on the stack to choose which routines to call.

name: run_cordic_loop_signed
description: Runs a shift-and-add loop over a table of constants on its argument and calls routines whose path depends on a sign value passed on the stack.

name: run_cordic_loop_branch

name: run_cordic_table_iteration

name: normalize_value_exponent_loop
description: Negates a negative value and, when it lies outside a small range, shifts its bits left until the top bit is set while adjusting an exponent counter. It returns once the top bit is set.

name: normalize_value_exponent_check
description: Returns early when a second operand's upper byte is minus one. Otherwise it normalises the value by shifting its bits left until the top bit is set and adjusting an exponent counter.

name: call_one_then_two

name: call_incremented_value_pair

name: build_mantissa_with_exponent

name: shift_loop_with_exponent_exit
description: Runs a bit-by-bit subtract-and-shift loop and, on exit, calls a routine. It then shifts a value left until its sign bit is set, using a shift count taken from the high byte of a stored argument, and calls two routines.

name: store_signed_shifted_value

name: store_shifted_value_checked
